theme: Housing-policy and STR-ban datasets: HOA/condo STR bans, NYC OSE enforcement data, Barcelona/Amsterdam/Paris enforcement, Spanish 2025 platform registration numbers

candidates.name: illegal-hotel-inspections
candidates.what_it_holds: inspections.csv: ~2,491 usable inspection records (2,684 original, 193 dropped as non-STR) from a WNYC FOIA request to the NYC Mayor's Office of Special Enforcement (predecessor to today's OSE), Oct 2013-Apr 2015. Fields cover property info, inspection reason/trigger, and violations found. 4 commits, last updated ~2015, no license listed.
candidates.why_useful: Direct historical NYC OSE enforcement microdata (this scout's core target and gap #12 regulatory tracker). Pre-dates our held NYC OSE dataset and could extend the enforcement-intensity time series further back (2013-15), useful as a base-period comparator for post-Local-Law-18 enforcement intensity.
candidates.last_activity: ~Sep 2015 (stale but data is a fixed historical FOIA extract)

candidates.name: vakantieverhuur-check
candidates.what_it_holds: A small HTML/JS tool (not a dataset) that tells a Dutch homeowner how many nights/year they may legally short-term-let before needing a permit, keyed by Dutch municipality (vakantieverhuur rules). Topics: airbnb, compliance, netherlands, short-term-rental. 0 stars, updated within the last week (Sep 2026), no license stated.
candidates.why_useful: Encodes per-municipality Dutch STR night-cap rules (a proxy for regulatory tightness feeding Amsterdam/NL enforcement severity), but it is a rules-lookup tool, not enforcement or registration data, so only marginally useful without scraping its rule table.
candidates.size_hint: small static site, unknown rule-table row count

candidates.name: Local-law-18-vs-Short-term-rentals
candidates.what_it_holds: Single-commit repo containing only 'Poster code.R' and 'poster.pdf' (an academic poster on NYC Local Law 18's effect on STRs). No committed data files, no README, no license.
candidates.why_useful: No usable data of its own; flagged only because it surfaced under Local Law 18 search terms. Not worth pursuing further.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: likely reuses Inside Airbnb NYC data we already hold

candidates.name: Price-of-Staying-in-the-Big-Apple
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter-notebook analysis of NYC Airbnb listings/reviews exploring the impact of Local Law 18 via unsupervised methods; per the description it works from listing/review data, almost certainly Inside Airbnb NYC dumps re-packaged rather than a new source. Last updated Oct 2025.
candidates.why_useful: Likely duplicates Inside Airbnb NYC data already held; only worth a line because it is a LL18-focused analysis (possible source of a derived pre/post-LL18 supply metric) rather than new raw data.

notes: Two severe access constraints this session: (1) the WebSearch tool reported the session's 200-query budget was already exhausted before my first call, so none of the assigned keyword-hint WebSearch queries could run; (2) GitHub's own search UI (fetched via WebFetch, not `gh`) rate-limits aggressively and inconsistently -- roughly 1 successful fetch per 60-90s wait, with some 429s carrying no Retry-After and persisting through multiple wait cycles. DuckDuckGo (regular + lite), Google, and Ecosia all returned CAPTCHA/403 pages to WebFetch; Bing rendered but ignored the site: operator and returned generic results; Zenodo and HuggingFace dataset search pages are JS-rendered and returned empty via WebFetch. Given these constraints I relied entirely on github.com/search?type=repositories fetched one at a time with waits between calls, which is a narrower net than the assigned WebSearch-based method (no Kaggle/awesome-list/blog-post discovery was possible). Substantive finding: this theme is thin on GitHub specifically -- Spanish/Barcelona/Amsterdam/Paris official STR registries and 2025 registration-number rollouts appear to live only on government open-data portals (not mirrored to GitHub), and HOA/condo STR bans are private governance documents with essentially no public dataset presence; the one solid hit (datanews/illegal-hotel-inspections) is a 2015-vintage NYC OSE FOIA extract that pre-dates and could extend our held OSE series. Recommend a follow-up scout with working WebSearch (fresh session/budget) specifically targeting: Barcelona Ajuntament open-data GitHub mirrors, Amsterdam Gemeente open-data org, Paris opendata.paris.fr meublés touristiques mirrors, and Spain's INE/Ministerio Vivienda registro unico de arrendamientos (RUAT/ventanilla unica) 2025 rollout -- none of these official-portal names returned anything on plain github.com/search, suggesting they need either the government-portal's own GitHub org name (unknown to me) or a working general web search to locate community mirrors.
